items.title: Publishers urge US court to reject OpenAI's fair use defence in copyright case
items.excerpt: Four publishing and copyright organisations, including the AAP and IBPA, filed an amicus brief urging a US court to reject OpenAI's fair-use defence, arguing AI training on copyrighted books threatens authors' livelihoods.
items.rationale: A new court filing: four publishing bodies, including the AAP and IBPA, filed an amicus brief against OpenAI's fair-use defence in the authors' case. It is a concrete step in the central AI-training dispute and is separate from the ROSS ruling published 10-06.

items.title: Rise in number of illustrators losing work to GenAI, survey finds
items.excerpt: An Association of Illustrators survey finds a growing number of illustrators losing work and income to generative AI, with the technology changing how much work they get and how commissions are briefed.
items.rationale: New Association of Illustrators survey data on lost commissions and income, which is directly relevant to book illustrators and cover designers. The ERR item from 09-30 was a publisher's opinion, not this data.

items.title: Stanford professors opt out of Anthropic settlement and file their own lawsuit over pirated books used to train Claude
items.excerpt: Stanford professors whose books were pirated to train Claude opted out of the $1.5 billion settlement and filed their own lawsuit against Anthropic.
items.rationale: Follow-up on the Anthropic settlement with a new event: authors who opted out have filed their own suit. This shows the opt-out-and-sue route that authors deciding on the $1.5B payout can take.

items.title: IFRRO Releases New Study on AI, Copyright Issues
items.excerpt: IFRRO's new report combines legal and market analysis of AI and copyright with a global survey of nearly 2,000 rightsholders and users.
items.rationale: A newly released global report from the reproduction-rights federation, with a survey of nearly 2,000 rightsholders and users. It is a different document from the Authors Guild guidelines published 10-17.

items.title: Brain Ventures lists webtoon-localization Photoshop plugin ToonFlow on Adobe Exchange
items.excerpt: AI webtoon-localization firm Brain Ventures listed ToonFlow, a Photoshop plugin that automates speech-bubble detection, OCR, translation and lettering, on Adobe Exchange.
items.rationale: The most actionable pick: a released tool, now on Adobe Exchange, that automates bubble detection, OCR, translation and lettering in Photoshop for comics and webtoon localization. No earlier ToonFlow story has run.

https://stanforddaily.com/2026/10/27/pro.new_action: Stanford professors opted out of the $1.5B Anthropic settlement and filed their own copyright lawsuit (a new court filing).
